sources: American Academy of Pediatrics, HealthyChildren.org (sleep, feeding, and media)
CDC Learn the Signs. Act Early. developmental milestones
NHS Start for Life and birth-to-five guidance

sleep.0-3: Many babies this age sleep in short stretches through the day and night, and often wake to feed. Lots of families put them down in a dark, quiet place.
sleep.4-6: Night sleep often gets longer around this age, and many babies still nap several times in the day. Families often use the same short wind-down each evening.
sleep.7-12: Many babies this age take two or three naps and still wake at night. Lots of families end the day with the same few bedtime steps.
sleep.13-18: Many toddlers this age still need one nap a day, and waking early still happens. Lots of families wind down with the same bedtime routine.
sleep.19-24: Many toddlers this age still nap once in the day, and bedtime protests are part of many evenings. It often helps to keep the same wind-down steps.
sleep.25-36: Some children this age still nap, and some are giving the nap up. Bedtime resistance shows up a lot, and many families answer it with a steady evening routine.
sleep.37-60: Many children this age have stopped napping. Stalling at bedtime and waking in the night still happen in a lot of families.

food.0-3: Milk feeds, often through the day and night, are how babies this age eat. Hunger often returns sooner than a clock suggests.
food.4-6: Milk is still the main food at this age. Many families start first foods around 6 months.
food.7-12: Many babies this age are learning to eat soft foods as well as milk, and a mess is part of that. Appetite often changes from one day to the next.
food.13-18: Many toddlers this age eat small meals and turn down foods they liked recently. Lots of families have meals together.
food.19-24: Lots of toddlers this age want the same few foods and refuse others. Many families offer a familiar food alongside something else.
food.25-36: Many children this age still prefer a few familiar foods. Meals can be short, and playing with food is part of it.
food.37-60: Many children this age eat with the family and still refuse some foods. Appetite often goes up and down across the week.

play.0-3: Watching a face, listening to a voice and short awake spells are how many babies this age play.
play.4-6: Reaching, mouthing objects and time on the floor fill a lot of play. A spell of it often lasts only a few minutes.
play.7-12: Banging, dropping and passing objects back and forth fill a lot of play. Many babies want the same little game over and over.
play.13-18: Filling and tipping containers, and playing beside other children, take up a lot of playtime. Play is often on the move.
play.19-24: Simple pretend play, such as feeding a doll or pushing a toy car, shows up for lots of toddlers. They often play near others more than with them.
play.25-36: Pretend play and very simple games with turns are a big part of play. Play can tip into frustration quickly.
play.37-60: Imaginative play and time with other children take up a lot of the day. Games with a few simple rules start to make sense to many children this age.

feelings.0-3: Crying is a main way babies this age say they need something. Settling often comes with holding, feeding or a change of position.
feelings.4-6: Many babies this age are more social, and may fuss when a familiar person leaves. A calm adult close by is often what settles them.
feelings.7-12: Caution around new people, and clinging to familiar ones, shows up a lot. Big cries over a small change happen too.
feelings.13-18: Big feelings come on fast, including a short meltdown when a toddler cannot manage something alone. Many adults stay close and calm.
feelings.19-24: Tantrums, and wanting to do things without help, are part of many days. A calm adult nearby often sees the moment pass.
feelings.25-36: Strong feelings about small changes come easily. Many adults name the feeling out loud.
feelings.37-60: Many children this age can say how they feel, and a big reaction to disappointment still happens. Time with a calm adult often helps the feeling pass.

talking.0-3: Cooing, crying and going quiet for a familiar voice are what many babies do. They also start to trade sounds back and forth.
talking.4-6: Babbling and turning toward a voice fill a lot of the day. Many babies enjoy hearing the same sounds again and again.
talking.7-12: Babbling with a wider mix of sounds is what many babies do, and a first word may appear. Understanding usually runs ahead of the words a baby can say.
talking.13-18: Many toddlers this age say a handful of words and understand far more than they say. Pointing and gestures carry a lot of what they mean.
talking.19-24: Many toddlers this age add words quickly, and phrases of two words start to appear. Understanding still runs ahead of speaking.
talking.25-36: Short sentences and lots of questions fill a lot of talk. People outside the family often find the speech hard to follow at this age.
talking.37-60: Many children this age speak in sentences and can tell a simple story about the day. Conversation goes back and forth more easily.

moving.0-3: Lifting the head during floor time and watching things that move take up a lot of awake time. Movement comes in short bursts.
moving.4-6: Rolling, reaching and pushing up on the arms during floor time show up for many babies. Each one gets there in their own time.
moving.7-12: Sitting, crawling and pulling up to stand show up in this stretch, and the timing varies a lot from one baby to another.
moving.13-18: Walking, climbing and tumbles all show up. Moving along the furniture often comes first.
moving.19-24: Running, climbing and kicking a ball take up a lot of play. Stairs are interesting, and many families offer a hand to hold.
moving.25-36: Jumping, running and trying stairs with a hand to hold fill a lot of active time. Balance is still developing.
moving.37-60: Hopping, climbing and riding a trike or scooter show up for many children this age. Coordination is still coming along.

care.0-3: Frequent nappy changes are part of the day. Baths are short, with an adult there the whole time.
care.4-6: Bath time is often a playful part of the day, with an adult there throughout. Nappy changes are still very frequent.
care.7-12: Many babies this age take an interest in getting dressed. An adult still stays within reach for the whole bath.
care.13-18: Lots of toddlers want to help with dressing and washing hands, and it often takes longer that way.
care.19-24: Many toddlers this age want to wash and dress themselves. Nappy or potty timing varies a lot from one child to another.
care.25-36: Interest in the potty shows up, and so does a wide range of timing. Accidents are part of this stretch for many families.
care.37-60: Many children this age use the toilet, and accidents still happen. Brushing teeth with an adult helping is what many families do.

outings.0-3: Short trips out, and a lot of time being carried, fill the early months. Many babies sleep on the way.
outings.4-6: Many babies this age like looking around on a trip, and some fuss on the way. Shorter outings tend to go more smoothly.
outings.7-12: Outings often go better when they stay short. Many babies this age want to see what is happening around them.
outings.13-18: Many toddlers this age want to walk some of the way and be carried the rest. A short trip with something to look at is what many families try.
outings.19-24: Wanting to walk, and tiring of a long trip, are part of many outings. A familiar toy and something to eat are how many families keep going.
outings.25-36: Many children this age manage a short outing and find a long wait hard. It often helps to say what comes next.
outings.37-60: Many children this age manage a longer outing when they know the plan. Waiting is still hard for a lot of them.

screens.0-3: Babies this age follow faces and voices close by. Screens are not a usual part of play at this age, apart from a live call with a familiar person.
screens.4-6: Babies this age learn from people and from objects they can touch. Screens are not a usual way to fill play at this age.
screens.7-12: People, voices and objects a baby can handle are still how this age learns. Screen use is uncommon as play.
screens.13-18: Children this age still learn most from people and from play. Screens are still an uncommon way to spend the day.
screens.19-24: Where families use a screen at this age, watching together and talking about it is what many of them do, and it stays brief.
screens.25-36: Many families keep screen time short and shared at this age. Play and conversation still fill most of the day.
screens.37-60: Many children this age watch a screen sometimes. Keeping it brief, with an adult watching too, is what many families do.
